correctness.rationale: Proof defines D and J with normalized arclength; energy conservation is exact. Finite-polynomial Hessian uses Parseval, and analytic Fourier constant-term expansion gives the full fourth and sixth coefficients and a strict positive optimized 1/24 sixth-order deficit. Verify script independently recomputes exact Laurent coefficients and numerical integrals. The orbit distance is asymptotic to square-root of two times absolute x, forcing the p<6 stability obstruction. No infinite-dimensional stability lower bound is inferred. At exponent six the limiting ratio is e/192, giving a necessary upper bound for any positive stability constant.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Frank–Ivanisvili gives a stronger global bound on function values, but strictness does not dominate a quantitative necessary stability exponent: it is compatible with arbitrarily flat near-maximizers. The 1994 analysis proves local monotonicity along fixed normalized lines, not the curved four-mode flattening.

value.rationale: The 2026 sharp global Chang–Marshall theorem makes near equality a natural open quantitative issue. The unique resonant z-cubed and z-fourth correctors expose a hidden sixth-order flatness and an explicit obstruction to every stability exponent below six in Dirichlet distance, a structural fact not obtainable from the known sharp constant or mere correctness of the symbolic computation. The same path gives the exact ceiling e/192 on any putative positive sixth-power stability constant.
